text:
elaine: Heads-up — I opened a small docs PR for the uploads endpoint. The current API reference shows a JSON body example for POST /v1/uploads but our runtime expects multipart/form-data for files. Can we update the curl and browser fetch examples? PR: #3214

sam: ah ok, saw that in the code review. The handler explicitly reads multipart. Good catch.

docs-bot: PR #3214 by elaine: docs: change /v1/uploads example to multipart; add FormData JS snippet (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3214) :rocket:

mike: +1. Also noticed the response example in the reference uses `file_id`. The service returns `upload_id` and `filename` now. Need to align the response schema block.

elaine: yep — I propose the minimal changes: 
1) curl example use `-F "file=@sample.txt"` and `-F "purpose=vector_index"`
2) add a small fetch/TS snippet with FormData
3) update response example from `{ "file_id": "..." }` to `{ "upload_id": "...", "filename": "..." }`

sam: draft curl snippet looks like: ```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/uploads" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -F "file=@./sample.txt" \
  -F "purpose=vector_index"
```
We should also keep a tiny JSON example for metadata-only uploads (e.g., reference URLs) — but keep the main example multipart.

elaine: good idea to keep the metadata-only example. I'll add a short note: "If you're uploading a remote resource by URL, you can POST JSON {\"url\": \"https://...\"} and the service will fetch it; binary files must be multipart form uploads."

mike: one more thing — the OpenAPI requestBody currently lists `content: application/json` only. We must add `multipart/form-data` with schema: `type: object`, properties `file: type: string, format: binary` and `purpose: { type: string }`. I can add that in the OpenAPI patch.

sam: I can handle the curl + fetch snippets and examples in the markdown. Mike, if you add the OpenAPI requestBody change that should cover the schema. Elaine, can you add a short migration note in the top-of-file change log pointing out the response field rename to `upload_id`?

elaine: sure. I'll add a line: "2026-03-22: Corrected uploads examples to use multipart/form-data; response `file_id` renamed to `upload_id` in runtime — update client code accordingly."

tolga: For the fetch example, use this TypeScript snippet: ```ts
const form = new FormData();
form.append('file', fileInput.files[0]);
form.append('purpose', 'vector_index');
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/uploads', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}` },
  body: form,
});
const data = await res.json();
console.log(data.upload_id, data.filename);
```
Add a note about not setting `Content-Type` manually when using FormData in browsers.

sam: perfect. Also add a tiny unit test pointer for the docs repo: `docs/test/samples/uploads-examples.md` with a step that runs the curl sample against local dev server. That helps catch regressions.

elaine: will do. I can push the markdown edits in the PR later today. 

mike: ping me when PR is ready. I'll add the OpenAPI change and run schema validation. :white_check_mark:

sam: sounds good. thanks all. small but important fix. :thumbsup:

docs-bot: Updated checklist for PR #3214: snippets added, openapi pending, changelog entry pending.

elaine: done — pushed edits and added the migration note. Ready for review.

mike: reviewing now. will merge once CI green.

sam: thx — after merge I'll coordinate a tiny announcement in release notes so SDKs can bump if needed.

elaine: bonus: I added a one-liner in the SDK migration guide: "When migrating from v1.3 -> v1.4, replace references to `file_id` with `upload_id` for the uploads endpoint."

mike: nice. ok merging in a bit.

elaine: thanks everyone.
